diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then we have $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L_N)$ for all $N\geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof infers membership in Range(L) from membership in every finite-dimensional Range(L_N) and the asserted range limit. Membership in all finite-dimensional approximants gives at most membership in the closure, not in Range(L). In fact, no pure character is in Range(L): the pushforward of u under y mapsto c^{-1} xhat dot y - t_0 is absolutely continuous on the corresponding interval, whereas Lu = e^{-i tau b} would force that pushforward to be the point mass delta_b. For example, with D the unit ball, xhat=e_1, c=1, t_0=eta=0 and z=0, the claimed identity would require 1 = integral_D e^{-i tau y_1} u(y) dy for all tau in [0,K], which is impossible for u in L^2(D).

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair is identified. At minimum, the pointwise exponential tests must be replaced by regularized tests for which the Picard finiteness criterion is genuinely equivalent to the strip condition, or the range characterization must be reformulated and the indicators redesigned; a new factorization or closure argument is required.
issues.overall_effect: The Picard-based indicators are infinite at every test point under the stated range criterion, so W and the later indicator functions vanish identically rather than characterizing the strips. The strip, pulse-moment, Theta-hull, convex-hull, and multiple-pulse conclusions lose their supporting factorization results.
issues.title: Pointwise exponential test functions are not in Range(L) inside the strip
issues.why_classification: The central range characterization is false as stated, and the advertised indicators and uniqueness theorems do not survive without essentially new test functions or a new factorization argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists} $ N_0 \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ such that  ${D} \subset \bigcup\limits_{m=1}^{N} B_{|D|/N}(y_m)$ for all $N>N_0$;
The last equality follows from the choice of $\{y_m\} ^{\infty}_{m=1}$ and the fact that $S\in C(\overline{D})$.

issues.failure_explanation: In R^3, |D| is a positive Lebesgue measure. N balls of radius |D|/N have total volume (4 pi/3) N (|D|/N)^3 = (4 pi/3)|D|^3/N^2, which is eventually smaller than |D|. Hence no sequence {y_m} can satisfy the displayed covering condition for all large N. Consequently the asserted Riemann-sum convergence of F_N to F has no admissible discretization points.

failure_location.quote: $ N_0 \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ such that  ${D} \subset \bigcup\limits_{m=1}^{N} B_{|D|/N}(y_m)$ for all $N>N_0$;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |D|/N by a feasible quasi-uniform radius, for example |D|^{1/3}/N in R^3, and re-prove the Riemann-sum convergence from that covering condition. This repairs only the discretization; the separate range-membership defect must still be repaired before Theorem lem3.4 can be salvaged.
issues.overall_effect: The discretization argument used in the proof of Theorem lem3.4 is unavailable as written. This is an additional independent defect in that proof, beyond the false range-membership claim in ISSUE-001.
issues.title: The discretization covering condition is infeasible in three dimensions
issues.why_classification: The hypothesis can be made feasible by a dimension-dependent covering radius and a corresponding quadrature estimate, so the repair is contained; however, it is not a mere typographical correction and does not by itself restore the theorem because of ISSUE-001.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $F^{(\hat x)}$ is a $N\times N$ complex matrix.
u^{\infty}({\hat x},\kappa+\omega_1) & u^{\infty}({\hat x},\kappa-\omega_1) & \cdots   & u^{\infty}({\hat x},\kappa-\omega_{N-1})

issues.failure_explanation: The far-field matrix is a complex Toeplitz approximation and is generally nonnormal. For a nonnormal matrix, the eigenvectors of F are not eigenvectors of |Re F| + |Im F|, and the eigenvalues of F_# are not obtained by replacing each eigenvalue of F by |Re lambda| + |Im lambda|. The claim would require normality or simultaneous diagonalizability of Re F and Im F, neither of which is established.

failure_location.quote: then one deduces that  an eigen-system of the matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#:= |\real (F^{(\hat x)})|+|\ima(F^{(\hat x)})|$ is $\left\{ ( \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n, \psi^{(\hat x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$, where $ \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n:=|\real (\tilde \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n)| +|\ima (\tilde \lambda^{( \hat x)}_n)|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute F_# directly from the self-adjoint matrices Re F and Im F using matrix absolute values, for example through their spectral decompositions or SVDs, or replace F by a normal/self-adjoint surrogate and restate the numerical guarantee accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The computed eigenpairs used in the discrete indicators are not guaranteed to be eigenpairs of the discrete F_#, so the numerical reconstruction procedure does not implement the stated factorization method.
issues.title: The numerical spectrum of F_# is incorrectly deduced from the spectrum of nonnormal F
issues.why_classification: The algorithmic guarantee fails as written, but it can be repaired by a contained change in the numerical linear algebra without altering the overall reconstruction strategy.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: u^{\infty}({\hat x},\kappa+\omega_1) & u^{\infty}({\hat x},\kappa-\omega_1) & \cdots   & u^{\infty}({\hat x},\kappa-\omega_{N-1})

issues.failure_explanation: With tau_n=n Delta omega and s_m=(m-0.5)Delta omega, the (n,m) frequency is kappa+(n-m+1/2)Delta omega. Thus the (1,3) entry should involve kappa-omega_3, not the kappa-omega_2 pattern displayed by the Toeplitz matrix. The same off-by-one shift affects the negative-frequency diagonals and the stated list of 2N-1 samples.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use one consistent grid, for example replace the (n,m) entry by u^infinity(x, kappa+(n-m+1/2)Delta omega) and adjust the sampled frequencies accordingly, or redefine the tau and s grids and the frequency samples so that the displayed Toeplitz formula is exact.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the matrix does not approximate the rectangular rule stated immediately before it, so the discrete far-field operator uses shifted frequency samples.
issues.title: The displayed Toeplitz matrix is inconsistent with the stated rectangular-rule grid
issues.why_classification: The inconsistency is local and has a direct indexing repair that preserves the numerical method once the same grid is used throughout.
